raw_segments.text: Of the former kind, are in England, the tax upon hawkers and peddlers, that upon hackney
coaches and chairs, and that which the keepers of ale-houses pay for a license to retail
During the late war, another tax of the same kind was proposed upon shops.
The war having been undertaken, it was said, in defense of the trade of the country, the
merchants, who were to profit by it, ought to contribute towards the support of it.
